Table of Contents PriyankaS3ri October 7, 2020 10:20 am Most Common Tableau Basic Interview Questions You Should Know Tableau is the more popular data visualization tool used for extensive data analysis. This was founded in 2003, later acquired by Salesforce in 2019. It can be used to convert unstructured data into useful information for the business. Moreover, this data interpretation can be easily understood by non-technical persons like people from sales and marketing. This information can be used by companies to understand the various market trends and take necessary corrective actions. Preparing for a data visualization role? Mastering Tableau interview questions is essential. Whether you’re a fresher or a professional, understanding key Tableau interview questions and answers can give you a strong edge in the hiring process. This guide covers frequently asked topics, including Tableau basic interview questions to help you build a solid foundation. For those ready to upskill with practical expertise and real-time projects, explore our Course On Tableau at 3RI Technologies—designed to equip you with job-ready skills and help you land your dream role in the data analytics field. Tableau’s significant demand in different industries has given rise to an increase in job opportunities for developers. Here, I am to help you prepare interviews to grab a job in this field. I have prepared this question with a lot of research. I hope this helps you. Tableau Scenario Based Interview Questions and Answers Q 1- What is meant by Tableau? It is a smart software used by various businesses to analyze raw data in the form of images, videos, and so on. The information collected is then transformed into meaningful data in a visual format like dashboards for easy understanding. It is also used to present the changes and density of this data in form of graphs. Using this system, we can easily blend and collaborate this real-time data for uniqueness. Q 2 – State the different data types supported in Tableau? Tableau can support strings, date, time, number, Boolean and geographical values. The data type of a field can be changed using Data pane/Data Source. Q 3- Differentiate between the traditional tools used for Business Intelligence and Tableau. Tableau: The architecture has no dependency on hardware. It is based on associative search which makes it faster. It supports advanced technologies like multi-threading, in-built memory, and so on. It is a cost-effective tool and easy to understand. Traditional tools for Business Intelligence: It has a dependency on hardware. It is based on complicated technology. It does not support advanced technologies like multi-threading, in-built memory, and so on. It does not support advanced technologies like multi-threading, in-built memory, and so on. Q 4- What are the different products offered by Tableau? Also, state the latest version. Tableau Desktop can be used to transform images into efficient queries. You can the form establish a connection between your desktop and data warehouse for analysis of data. It can be used to produce a dashboard. Tableau Server can be used to share the dashboard generated by the Tableau desktop over the web. It will give quick access to published content. Tableau Online is a system that is deployed in a cloud environment. You can easily access the published dashboards using a mobile app or browser. There is not required to set up the hardware. Tableau Reader is used to only read the files in Tableau. You cannot edit any dashboard created by Tableau. Tableau Public is a free version of Tableau. You can create your dashboard and other visualizations but can’t save them on your local machine. Tableau 2020.3.1 is the latest version released on 30th September 2020. Q 5- Differentiate between Measures and Dimensions. Measures: It is related to numbers and quantities of data like Profit, Loss, and so on. It can be collected. It contains a foreign key, which refers to the corresponding dimension, ion table. Dimensions: It is related to the qualities of data like name, geographical information, date, etc. It is used to classify, divide, and disclose the data. It has a reference to the measures table. Q 6- What is the maximum size of the file allowed in Tableau? There is no maximum size limit for files in Tableau. Want to Upskill to get ahead in your career? Check out the Tableau Online Training Q 7- What are the different file extensions available with Tableau? .twb(Tableau Workbook), .twbx(Tableau Packaged Workbook), .tde(Tableau Data Extract), .tbm(Tableau Bookmark, .tds(Tableau Data Source), .tms(Tableau Map Source), .tdsx(Tableau Packaged Data Source), .tps(Tableau Preferences) are the different file extensions in Tableau. Q 8- Differentiate between .twb and .twbx extensions. .twb: It is an XML file It contains all selection and layout that has been used in the workbook of Tableau It contains no data .twbx: It is a zipped file It includes a .twb file along with some other files like images of the background, and so on. It only contains other files Q 9- What is meant by a filter and state the different types of filters used in Tableau? A filter is a mechanism by which we can prevent unwanted data from appearing in Tableau’s workbook and dashboard. The different types of filters are Context, Data Source, and Extract filters. It also has a filter on Measure, Dimension, and Table Calculations. Q 10- What is the Level Of Detailed Expression? It is used whenever we want to run complicated queries related to several dimensions where data is sourced. Although I am providing you with Top 50 Tableau Interview questions, I would personally enroll for Tableau Online Training at 3RI Technologies to get trained by expert working professionals in flexible batch timings. Q 11- What is TreeMap? TreeMap is a technique by which data is organized sequentially in descending order. It shows them in a set of rectangles. Parent rectangles follow child rectangles. Q 12- What is Heat Map? It is a technique by which different colours are used to represent different sets of data. Higher values are indicated with darker colours. Q 13- What is the Tableau dashboard? It is a representation of different data that can be used for studying additional data simultaneously. Any change in data brings modification to the dashboard. Q 14- What is a story in Tableau? It is a collection of dashboards and datasheets that can be used to reveal the interpretation of data. This is used in making decisions by analyzing the facts and their results. Q 15- Different connection types in Tableau? The extract is a representation of data that is derived from the data source and inserted into the repository. Live is a direct connection between the source of data and the tables from where data is fetched. This gives consistent data all the time. Q 16- State the different joints used in Tableau? Inner Join, Full Outer Join, Left, and Right Outer Join are the different joins available. Q 17- The maximum number of tables that able to be joined using Tableau? Thirty-two tables can be joined at the most in Tableau. Q 18- What is the use of Data Modelling? It is the initial stage of Object-oriented programming. It is used to analyze the data and identify the relationship between objects of data. Q 19- How can you improve the performance of Tableau? Workbooks can work faster with the use of Extracts. The data considered for analysis can be reduced. You can use fewer marks on views so that information is not overloaded. You can hide unnecessary, unused fields and use context filters. You may use indexing, and unwanted calculations can be removed from the sheet. These Top 50 Tableau Interview questions would help you in your preparation for interviews. I would want you to learn Tableau from the Pioneers in Tableau Training in Pune at 3RI Technologies. Interested to begin a career in Tableau? Enroll now for SQL And Tableau Certification Q 20- What is meant by shelves in Tableau? It is the labelled area to the left and top of the window in Tableaus like Page Shelf, Filter Shelf, Mark Shelf, Row, and Column Shelf. Q 21- What is meant by Sets in Tableau? These are customized fields that will define a particular set of data fulfilling a specific condition. For example, a set of customers who purchase on or before a particular date. Q 22- What is meant by Groups in Tableau? It is a collection of dimension members to form a category of high level. For example, showing only people who have purchased Samsung Microwave Convection 28 litre oven. Q 23- What is the disadvantage of using a context filter in Tableau? Whenever a context filter is created, a temporary table is created every time the view is created. Any change in the context filter needs an update in a temporary table affecting the performance. Q 24- What is the published data source? If we want our data source on the tableau desktop to be made available to other users, we can publish them using Tableau Online. This can be also done by making an embedded text or excel file. Q 25- What is Mark Card? It can be found to the left of your view. You can easily drag and control fields like colour, shape, size, and so on. Q 26- What is Dual-Axis? It is used to compare two measures simultaneously. Websites like Naukri.com uses it to compare growth in a different industry. Q. 27- What is Bullet Graph? It is used to compare one measure field with another using a bar graph. Q 28- Define hierarchical field. It is used to view data more finely. Q 29- What is the use of the Data Engine in Tableau? It is used to receive responses quickly, improve performance, and collaborated with the existing data system. The data is stored in disks during imports, so RAM is not used often. It speeds up the entire process. Q 30- What is Data Server in Tableau? It is a link between users in Tableau and data. It will permit you to load and share data. It saves the data connections, calculations, and field metadata that can be reused using them. Q 31- How to install Tableau Public? Go to https://public.tableau.com/s/ website to download for Windows or Mac Desktop. Enter the email id. Enter the same. Then click on Download App. The file is downloaded in your download folder set for the browser. Double click the file and follow the instructions to install. Once done, a desktop icon will be created. Double click on the same to open the Tableau Public. Q 32- State the difference between the Tiled and Floating layout. Tiled layout : In this type of design, the items will not overlap with each other. It always according to the size of the dashboard. Floating layout : The items may overlap with each other in case of space shortage. The items can have a fixed position, unlike Tiled Layout. Q 33- What is meant by VIZQL in Tableau? VIZQL stands for Visual Inquiry Language. It is like the SQL language. However, unlike querying data in SQL, it is used to convert data queries into images. Q 34- What is the meaning of aggregation and disaggregation of data in Tableau? Aggregation means producing a summary of data and viewing a single number—for example, the count of students in a class. Disaggregation means viewing all transactions used to analyze all measures dependent or independent of each other—for example, the salary of each employee. Q 35- What are the components of a dashboard? Web: It includes the web page, which is seen on the dashboard. Vertical component: It is a container in a vertical layout where you can add the desired objects. Horizontal component: It is a container in a horizontal layout where you can add the selected items. Text: it is the region where you can write and edit the desired text. Image Extract: Here, you can upload an image from the computer to the dashboard. I have prepared these Tableau Interview Questions and answers after extensive research. But this alone might not be sufficient for clearing an interview. It would help if you enrolled at 3RI Technologies for Data Analytics Courses in Pune Q 36- Steps to be followed while doing performance testing in Tableau? For a start: Go to the Help tab, click Settings and Performance, Start Performance Recording. For stop: Go to the Help tab, click Settings and Performance, Stop Performance Recording Q 37- Why should we use Tableau? It is simple to use and user friendly. It is used to manage a large set of data and integrate with multiple platforms. The complex graphs in Tableau look like simple pivots in Excel. The blending of data is easy to create their views to be shared with customers. It is easy to create visuals and switch between them. Q 38- Steps to be followed while creating a calculated field in Tableau? Select the Analysis tab, click the Calculated field from the drop-down. Calculation Editor Dialog box opens, provide a name to the Calculated field. Provide the formula in the editor. Click OK Now you will be able to see the newly added Calculated field in the data pane. Q 39- Can we give as many parameters as we want in Tableau? No, Parameters can be represented in four ways. It doesn’t allow passing more than one value in parameters. Q 40- What are some factors that are the reason for low performance in Tableau? Filter creation needs an additional query. So if you have more filters used inefficiently can drastically affect the performance. If an incorrect data source triggers a query for data, it will reduce the performance. Q 41- How can the parameters used in Tableau? Filter Action Calculated Field Measure-swaps Changing views Auto updates Q 42- Are there any data limitations in Tableau? Yes, 10 million rows are only allowed for the visualization of data. Q 43- Is it possible to download the workbook or view it from the server? Yes, we can easily download any workbook or view it from the server. But the format in which they can be downloaded depends on the permissions given by the admin or owners of the content. It can be downloaded as .png or .csv file. A.pdf file format can be used while downloading, but the web page’s objects are not included. Q 44- Can we use some columns which are a part of the data source, but not included in Reports? Yes, it is allowed. At times we use some columns in reports and some columns only as a filter. Q 45- What is the advantage of using Tableau extract? Tableau extract can be built and used without connecting to the database. Q 46- Can MS Excel files be placed in a shared location and used to create reports? Yes, but it would be better to extract a file for better performance. Q 47- How can testing be done in Tableau? We can use the Tableau Desktop application for testing. Q 48- Design a view that will show the population of different sex of each city in a particular state. The desired data must be present on the same sheet. Double click on the field for State. Drag the desired city to the desired State field. Drag no of males into the size field. Drag no of females into the colour field. Click on the size field and increase it to 80% Right-click the State field, and click Show Filter. Select Males and Females. Now you will be able to view Size as Males and Color as Females for each State. Q 49- Can we protect data in Tableau public? No, we cannot protect the data in Tableau public. Anyone can access this data. Q 50- Can relational joins be created without creating a new table? Yes, we can quickly create relational joins.
